name: pelvic pain overview
title: Pelvic pain decision chart: acute pain sorted by beta-hCG, fever and hemoglobin into ovarian torsion or ruptured hemorrhagic cyst; chronic pain sorted by cycle and exam into primary dysmenorrhea or structural causes (endometriosis, adenomyosis, leiomyoma, endometrial polyp); each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order

root.title: Pelvic pain: ACUTE (find the life- or limb-threat first) or CHRONIC (≥ 6 MONTHS)?
lines: history + physical exam come first: the most important part of any approach
chronic = below the umbilicus, ≥ 6 months, disabling or needing treatment · up to 50% have experienced abuse or trauma

groups.title: ACUTE: work it up in this order
lines: 1 · quantitative β-hCG: POSITIVE → ECTOPIC (FIRST-TRIMESTER BLEEDING chart)
2 · FEVER + white count ↑ → PID (SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS chart)

groups.title: CHRONIC: is it CYCLIC with a NORMAL exam?
lines: YES → functional (primary) · NO, or an exam/imaging finding → STRUCTURAL (secondary), more common with AGE

tiers.title: β-hCG < 1 · afebrile: is the hemoglobin STABLE?
lines: group and screen · repeat the CBC if bleeding may be ongoing

tiers.title: NO: STRUCTURAL · the EXAM points the way
lines: NODULAR, FIXED → endometriosis · BOGGY, tender, enlarged → adenomyosis · ENLARGED, MOBILE, mass → fibroid · MASS at the os → polyp

head: h
Ovarian torsion
ovary ± tube twists on its ligaments
SURGICAL EMERGENCY: save the ovary
pres: after VIGOROUS activity: intercourse, golf, exercise
inv: enlarged ovaries tort far more: a weighted pendulum
benign vs malignant: PELVIC MASS chart

head: h
Ruptured hemorrhagic ovarian cyst
UNCOMMON: most ruptures bleed little
inv: REPEAT it if bleeding may be ongoing

head: h
Primary dysmenorrhea
painful menses, NO structural cause
pres: CRAMPS on the first 1–2 days of flow
EASE as the period goes on

head: h
Endometriosis
endometrial tissue OUTSIDE the uterus
ovaries #1 · uterine ligaments #2
pres: dysmenorrhea · DEEP dyspareunia · dyschezia · dysuria · INFERTILITY
severity does NOT match the pain
~often NORMAL: does not rule it out
inv: many will not raise it unprompted
ANY 2 OF 3: endometrial glands · stroma · hemosiderin
tx: pseudopregnancy: OCP, ring, patch, Depo, IUS, Visanne
NOT first line · NOT if fertility wanted

head: h
Adenomyosis
endometrium DEEP in the myometrium
PAROUS · 40s–50s
inv: the glands are too deep · often found at hysterectomy

head: h
Leiomyoma (fibroid)
benign smooth-muscle NEOPLASM
NOT pre-malignant
pres: frequency, constipation · infertility if it DISTORTS THE CAVITY
tx: combined hormonal · Depo · Mirena · GnRH agonist
large or pedunculated → myomectomy or hysterectomy
pregnancy after it: case reports only

head: h
Endometrial polyp
benign, HORMONE-dependent overgrowth of endometrium
linked to estrogen, TAMOXIFEN · common > 40
pres: PAIN only if it protrudes through the os
small fleshy MASS at the cervical os
inv: 1 · REMOVE it: pathology makes the diagnosis
like the background endometrium, or HYPERPLASTIC (linked to endometrial hyperplasia)
tx: tell her: not a tumour; pathology confirms benign and excludes malignancy

panels.title: Fertility wishes change the plan
items: affects fertility: endometriosis · cavity-distorting fibroids · polyps · NOT adenomyosis
fibroid + wants pregnancy → myomectomy, not embolization
endometriosis + wants pregnancy → laparoscopic excision, not hysterectomy · avoid endometrioma surgery (costs ovarian reserve)

panels.title: Also on the differential
items: MYOFASCIAL pelvic pain: NOT cyclic · GLOBALLY tender pelvis, normal uterus → physiotherapy (soft-tissue release), trigger-point injection, amitriptyline + gabapentin
non-gynecologic: appendicitis, irritable bowel, interstitial cystitis, pelvic floor myalgia
